candidates.title: Statistical Jump Model (SJM) Asset-Specific Regime-Switching Nested Clustered Risk Parity
candidates.counterparty_mechanism: Slow-moving institutional 60/40 and static risk-parity mandates that cannot reallocate quickly when cross-asset stock-bond correlation flips positive or individual asset classes enter bear regimes.
candidates.economic_rationale: Static risk parity and blunt SMA200 switches suffer either from 2022-style simultaneous stock-bond drawdowns or noisy Gaussian-HMM whipsaw. Asset-specific Statistical Jump Models (SJMs) penalize spurious state transitions via an explicit jump penalty (lambda) to detect persistent calm vs turbulent states per asset before feeding regime-conditioned covariance estimates into Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) / Hierarchical Risk Parity across equities, sovereign bonds, gold, commodities, credit, and USD cash equivalents.

candidates.title: Forward-Looking VIX/VIX3M Term-Structure VRP & Multifactor Volatility-Managed Allocation with Deadband
candidates.counterparty_mechanism: Institutional equity hedgers and risk-averse pension allocators paying persistent option crash-insurance premia (implied vol > subsequent realized vol; VIX < VIX3M contango) while failing to adjust factor leverage when variance spikes.
candidates.economic_rationale: Building on Moreira & Muir (JF 2017) and 2024-2026 real-time multifactor extensions (DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera & Uppal, JF 2024; Reschenhofer & Zechner, JOIM/SSRN 2024-2025; Liu, SSRN 2026), jointly conditioning smart-beta equity factors (MTUM, QUAL, USMV, VTV, SPY, QQQ) on BOTH realized factor variance AND forward-looking option-implied term structure (IDX_VIX / IDX_VIX3M) overcomes backward-looking realized-vol lag. Adding an explicit L1 rebalancing deadband and cash/T-bill (BIL/SHY) safe-harbor directly targets the two known defects of Naqex Lab #4 (high 42.5x turnover and 2022 TLT duration trap), while Akula (Zenodo 2026) serves as a skeptical red-team benchmark against disguised plain-VRP beta.

candidates.title: Cross-Sectional Crypto Perpetual Funding-Crowding Carry x Slow (>= 4H/D1) Momentum Overlay
candidates.counterparty_mechanism: Leveraged retail and directional crypto speculators paying persistent 8-hour perpetual funding premia during crowded positioning while creating basis/momentum unwinds when arbitrage capacity tightens.
candidates.economic_rationale: Perpetual futures anchor to spot via path-dependent 8-hour funding transfers (He et al., arXiv:2212.06888v7; Kim & Park, arXiv:2506.08573). Recent 2026 empirical studies document both conditional arbitrage capacity limits in perpetual funding (Shek, SSRN 7520320) and net-of-costs cross-sectional momentum on tradable Binance perpetuals (Arefev, SSRN 7404139). Because Naqex Lab #9 already proved high-turnover taker altcoin carry fails once funding compresses, this frontier candidate tests a LOW-TURNOVER (>= D1 rebalance, hysteresis band, cross-margin only) joint Carry-Momentum signal: combining persistent funding-carry rank + spot-perp basis deviation + slow (>= 4H/D1) causal momentum on Tier-1 liquid coins, strictly excluding < 4H taker execution and capping total CEX exposure <= 25%.

candidates.title: Institutional Month-End Equity-Bond Rebalancing & Treasury Duration-Index Flow Premia
candidates.counterparty_mechanism: Trillions of USD in balanced 60/40 funds, target-date pension mandates, and government bond index trackers compelled to rebalance overweight/underweight equity-bond drifts and extend duration on rigid calendar month-end settlement dates.
candidates.economic_rationale: Non-informational institutional plumbing creates recurring, predictable price pressures at month boundaries: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone (NBER w33554, 2025) document that when equities are overweight vs bonds, mechanical institutional rebalancing sells stocks and buys bonds with measurable next-day price impact (~17 bps in their sample); Andonov, Jansen & Rauh (NBER w35896, 2026) trace liquidity-driven selling by negative-cash-flow pension funds; Soebhag, Verwijmeren & Martinetti (SSRN 7601879, 2026) isolate government bond index duration-rebalancing price pressure; and Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (RFS 2019/2020) establish the Dash-for-Cash turn-of-month reversal cycle. Trading ONLY the conditional equity-bond drift window (T-5..T-1) and turn-of-month settlement reversal (T-1..T+3) on liquid ETFs (SPY/QQQ vs TLT/IEF, parking in BIL/SHY ~70% of the month) yields ultra-low time-in-market and minimal correlation with both PORT_7E and continuous trend/VRP sleeves.

candidates.title: Multiscale Correlation-Gated Cross-Sector Dispersion Spread (Dollar-Neutral 10-Sector ETFs + Split-Session Tail Guard)
candidates.counterparty_mechanism: Passive index ETF and macro-herding flows that drive uniform beta shocks during high-correlation stress while leaving slow cross-sector fundamental rotation under-arbitraged during low-correlation, high-dispersion regimes.
candidates.economic_rationale: Cross-sector dispersion and pairwise correlation regimes separate idiosyncratic sector alpha from systemic macro beta (Bondarenko & Bernard, JFQA, doi:10.1017/s0022109023000960; Dolfin et al., arXiv:2408.17200, 2024). Because Akula (Zenodo 2026) warns that naive dispersion proxies often disguise plain VRP beta, and Naqex Lab #7 proved daily MOC-MOO overnight flips fail under transaction costs (0/4 killed), this mechanism constructs a strictly LOW-TURNOVER (monthly/bi-weekly) dollar-neutral Long Top-3 vs Short Bottom-3 US Sector Residual-Momentum spread across 10 SPDR ETFs (XLB..XLY, XLRE) that ONLY activates when causal 20-day pairwise sector correlation is below its rolling 75th percentile (high dispersion) and scales down using split-session overnight-vs-intraday tail heterogeneity diagnostics (Glasserman et al., arXiv:2507.04481, 2025; Chen, Hansen & Tong, arXiv:2607.03669, 2026). Dollar neutrality keeps expected correlation near zero against BOTH PORT_7E and directional ETF sleeves S3B/S4.
